reasons: Claim about O. Reg. 129/04 overall responsible operator licensing accurately reflects the requirement that the ORO hold an applicable licence of the same or higher class than the facility, matching s. 15(1).

Statement that an operator-in-training cannot be designated as overall responsible operator is directly traceable to s. 15(3) of O. Reg. 129/04 and correctly framed as an Ontario regulatory condition.
Jurisdiction and regulatory scope are correctly identified as Ontario wastewater operator licensing under O. Reg. 129/04, with no conflation with other provinces or U.S. EPA materials.

Exactly one option is correct; the distractors present plausible but incorrect scenarios (time-limited designation, Class I facilities with phone contact, owner authorization alone) without encouraging unsafe operation or omission of required regulatory oversight.

The learning objective—understanding that an OIT cannot be designated as ORO under Ontario Regulation 129/04—is foundational and appropriate for an Ontario OIT learner, focusing on basic regulatory role limits rather than advanced process control or design.
